originality.rationale: The new focus is the evaluated sharp long-time mode-exchange/noncancellation classification and local cubic-cusp switching-rate inverse for a delayed cross-particle fourth-order observable. Biroli et al. (arXiv:2312.02570, 2023) establish same-time variance-mixture distributions and squared-position correlations; the source full text and supplement were inspected. Biroli et al. (arXiv:2508.07199, 2025, revised 2026) study static collective statistics and ordinary two-time linear correlations but not the stated delayed fourth-order result. Behme, Di Tella and Sideris (arXiv:2207.11093, 2022; revised 2024) give a general Markov-modulated generalized OU autocovariance representation that can derive the unclassified conditional-variance covariance, which is not claimed new. Their general theorem does not explicitly state the evaluated nonzero double-pole threshold or the identifiable short-lag derivative ratio in the Brownian-gas observable. Relevant semantic literature searches did not disclose a stated equivalent classification. An equivalent specialization derived elsewhere from the broad MMGOU theory remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: The physically natural delayed squared-position covariance is the first nonzero cross-particle temporal correlator when each coordinate is centered and independent conditional on the shared trap. Its sharp mode exchange separates environmental relaxation from confined variance relaxation, including a genuine critical polynomial prefactor. The cubic nonanalyticity of an even fourth-order correlation, invisible in linear cross-correlation, provides an exact diffusivity-free readout of the switching rate for known stiffnesses. These are physically motivated full-parameter results, not arbitrary numeric evaluations; no estimator precision or unrelated application is asserted.
